report:
R1
- Behavior: Replace the hard-coded `EXPECTED_POST_CUTOFF` basename comparison with one oracle that classifies candidates from the sealed cutoff: frozen construction identity membership plus the sealed discovery predicates/filesystem boundaries and exact candidate identity. Partition the live walk all-and-only through that oracle; basename alone never establishes post-cutoff status.
- Deepest Owner: `test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts`, specifically its fixed-target construction-walk test and local sealed-predicate/candidate-identity functions.
- Red: Pass the same oracle a synthetic omitted frozen/pre-cutoff identity whose basename is `coder.ts` and require rejection. This counterexample exercises the real assertion path and defeats the former basename allowlist.
- Green: The real source root produces 597 matched, 0 missing, 0 changed and the exact cutoff-derived partition; every accepted addition has identity evidence proving absence from the sealed pre-cutoff identity set, while the omitted pre-cutoff `coder.ts` is rejected.
- Scope: Change only the existing verifier for this regression. Add no parallel verifier/helper, do not recut the denominator, inspect payloads, or alter frozen migration evidence.

R2
- Behavior: Implement one closed, canonical association grammar in the existing verifier. Its source universe is exactly: (a) frozen `inventory.json`/construction metadata for each of the 597 item keys, limited to `itemKey`, `basename`, and provenance/genericity/admission fields needed to select bytes; and (b) every byte source admitted for an item classified non-generic—repository bytes resolved from that item’s sealed reference tuple, and recovered/genuinely external source bytes bound by item key and sealed source SHA-256. Recursively omit every property named `issuePrCommitAssociations` and its descendants; persisted disposition/recovered-index association fields are comparison outputs only. Reject generic JSONL/session/tool-event items before opening payload bytes.

  Bind the sole repository namespace to `github.com/Akagilnc/ak-pi-workflow-roles`. Derive and cross-check that value from immutable Git bytes at `ea64733e382c6dcf14906b3b52782ec3f1c07535`: `.ak/dockets/issues/15/authority/judge-003/inputs/issue-snapshot` (`repository_url`/`html_url`) and `.ak/dockets/issues/15/migration/legacy-case-a/discovery-spec.v1.json` (`remoteHint: Akagilnc/ak-pi-workflow-roles`). Ledger both files as repository/full-commit/path/blob-OID/SHA-256 tuples. A mismatch is failure; no ambient remote/ref or other repository supplies namespace identity.

  Freeze ASCII lexical productions. Let `N = [1-9][0-9]*`, `H = [0-9A-Fa-f]{7,40}`, `B = [A-Za-z0-9_]`, and ASCII horizontal whitespace be `[ \t]`. Basenames accept only `(?:^|[-_.])issue[-_]N(?=$|[-_.])` and `(?:^|[-_.])pr[-_]N(?=$|[-_.])`, ASCII case-insensitively; thus the token must have an explicit start/end or `-`, `_`, `.` boundary on each outside edge. Text issue/PR labels accept only `(?:^|[^B])(issue|pr|pull[ \t]+request)[ \t]+#?N(?=$|[^0-9])`, ASCII case-insensitively; the left boundary is start or one ASCII character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, and the numeric right boundary is end or a non-ASCII-digit. Bare numbers and bare `#N` do not match.

  Qualified URLs accept only an ASCII URL token whose exact prefix is `https://github.com/Akagilnc/ak-pi-workflow-roles/`, followed by exactly `issues/N` or `pull/N`; its left edge is start or a character outside `[A-Za-z0-9._~:/?#@!$&'()*+,;=%-]`, and after `N` must be end or one of `#`, `?`, or a character outside that URL-character class. Host/owner/repository comparison is ASCII case-insensitive but canonicalizes to the namespace above. A different scheme, host, owner, repository, route, embedded URL token, or digit immediately following `N` is rejected.

  Recursive JSON structural extraction remains separate: positive decimal issue values are accepted only at exact ASCII-case-insensitive keys `issue`, `issueNumber`, or `issue_number`; PR values only at `pr`, `prNumber`, `pr_number`, `pullRequest`, `pullRequestNumber`, or `pull_request`; commit values only at `commit`, `commitOid`, `commitSha`, `headSha`, `reviewedHead`, or `targetHead`. Number values must be positive safe integers; string issue/PR structural values must be exactly `N`; string commit structural values must be exactly `H`. Independently, every recursive non-excluded JSON string value—including strings under unlisted keys and strings nested in objects/arrays—is scanned with exactly the same text-label, qualified-URL, and labeled-commit grammar used for Markdown/plain text. Structural listed-key extraction does not suppress or broaden that string scan, and results are set-deduplicated.

  Markdown/text and recursive JSON strings accept a commit only as `(?:^|[^B])(commit|commitOid|commitSha|headSha|reviewedHead|targetHead)[ \t]*[:=][ \t]*H(?=$|[^A-Za-z0-9])`, ASCII case-insensitively. The label must be immediately followed, apart from optional ASCII horizontal whitespace, by a literal colon or equals sign and then optional horizontal whitespace plus the token. Prose that merely mentions a commit field name—including `commitOid` or `reviewedHead`—without that immediate colon/equal labeled token is rejected. Unlabeled hex, hex under unlisted structural keys, embedded hex, non-hex, fewer than 7 or more than 40 hex digits, and arbitrary prose are rejected.

  Full commits require exactly 40 hex digits. Abbreviations require 7–39 digits and resolve uniquely only in the explicit commit universe reachable from the four sealed roots `ea64733e382c6dcf14906b3b52782ec3f1c07535`, `702e36f97caa92f012470bf5a890e656a5859800`, `49807d493861b5dc5e9c6a9813b2d7679a241df8`, and `da250445d09ef2b9105a99590f2ccda0a8db29c4` in the sealed local repository. Ambiguous/unresolvable abbreviations fail to associate. Lower-case commits and canonicalize/sort/deduplicate `{issues,pullRequests,commits}`; return null only when all sets are empty.
- Deepest Owner: The closed extractor, source selector, canonicalizer, resolver, and exact-set comparator in `test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts`; persisted outputs remain owned only by `.ak/dockets/issues/15/migration/legacy-case-a/dispositions.json` and `recovered-index.json`.
- Red: Table-drive every accepted and rejected boundary above through the same extractor/resolver used for real items, including basename edge characters, label boundaries, URL namespace/boundaries, nested JSON strings, listed versus unlisted structural keys, prose-only commit-field mentions, colon/equal commit labels, and ambiguous/unresolvable OIDs. Clone the actual parsed disposition/recovered record for second item `33454566…`, mutate its real `issuePrCommitAssociations` value, and run it through the identical canonical exact-set comparator; require mismatch. Also mutate an eligible parsed source input for that item to a rejected boundary and require its derived set/comparison to change. Do not delete an expected-map entry. Retain the first known-item check so both persisted metadata paths are exercised.
- Green: The bounded source universe deterministically derives one exact set per item; eligible frozen metadata, nested JSON structural values, every recursive JSON string, Markdown/text, recovered/external bytes, and referenced Git bytes are processed under the closed grammar. Both persisted files equal canonical sets exactly; accepted boundaries match, rejected boundaries remain absent, and both actual second-item mutations fail. Update only association fields whose values differ. No generic/excluded payload is opened.
- Scope: Change the existing verifier and only association fields in the two current migration metadata files. Do not alter source/derivative/report bytes, broaden the grammar during Apply, use ambient refs/remotes, inspect generic payloads, or change unrelated migration facts.

R3
- Behavior: Append a repair-003 Recorder closure with one independently executable child, result, and manifest/identity ledger. The child independently reruns corrected R1 and actual `scanBytes`; selection, dispositions, derivatives, and reports load from immutable Git inputs. Before import/execution it resolves and verifies exact scanner-module bytes. The ledger records repository identity/full commit/path/blob OID/SHA-256 for every Git-resolvable discovery spec, walk, inventory, disposition, report, scanner, derivative, association-resolution input, immutable namespace input, and other repository input; every genuinely external source records item key, source SHA-256, and applicable frozen identity metadata only.
- Deepest Owner: New `.ak/dockets/issues/15/repair/repair-003/recorder-closure/` evidence: the child owns execution gates and the manifest owns immutable attribution.
- Red: Through the child’s assertion path, perturb representative tuple components, scanner hash, selection identity, source seal, complete hit report, cutoff identity, namespace binding, and each known-redacted record and require failure/nonzero. The sole verifier mechanically exercises these gates against stored successor evidence.
- Green: The child exits 0 only for 597 matched/0 missing/0 changed, a cutoff-derived all-and-only partition, exactly 277 selected sources, verified scanner bytes, matching source/derivative hashes and complete hit reports, and both redactions. Every tuple/seal resolves and hashes, association/namespace resolution inputs are sealed, and no raw external-source duplicate is retained.
- Scope: Append only the new successor. Preserve repair-002 manifest, implementation, and result byte-for-byte, including seals `fd219ea9e1d43aae383d67a0289a92612726980e62b6a1aaf97fdacb19411576` and `654fdff4002b26cdaf08586b722aff6688b8c19b08752a62d329a84ef40e9a70`; preserve all earlier evidence. Do not share implementation with the seam verifier or retain scratch probes.

R4
- Behavior: Extend the sole verifier to resolve every successor Git tuple, verify every external seal/frozen-metadata binding and sealed association/namespace-resolution input, verify corrected exact association sets and actual red mutations, and enforce preservation of all historical evidence at the forward target.
- Deepest Owner: Acceptance assertions in `test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts`, backed by the repository `typecheck` script and new Recorder child/result gates.
- Red: Any tuple/seal mutation, association input/output mutation, namespace mutation, historical blob/hash mutation, repair-002 seal mutation, source-count drift, source identity loss/change, scanner drift, incomplete hit report, missing redaction, or non-forward target fails the focused verifier or child. If any required 597 historical identity or 277 external identity is missing/changed, stop with evidence-bearing refusal rather than substitute a cutoff or denominator.
- Green: At a new strict forward descendant, `npm run typecheck` and `node --import tsx --test test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts` pass; the successor records child exit 0; every ledger and grammar-boundary check passes; all four immutable commits remain ancestors; the four Receipt/manifest blob+SHA identities in `historical-nonconformance.json` re-resolve unchanged; and both repair-002 seals remain exact.
- Scope: Verification and preservation only. Do not change prior migration source bytes or any prior repair/Receipt/manifest/exhibit/result/historical-nonconformance bytes; no history rewrite, Case B, issues 16/17, session retention, generic/excluded-payload inspection, raw-source duplication, parallel verifier, or Soul/runtime/schema work. Planning was read-only on a clean worktree; no edit or commit was made.
